walkthroughs.body_html:
A change in magnetic flux through a coil induces an emf.

Faster change or more turns -> larger emf.

Current in coil in field -> turning force.

Split-ring reverses current each half-turn so motor keeps spinning.

Spinning a coil in a field induces an emf.

Generators in power stations make AC at 50 Hz.

mcqs.q: What produces a magnetic field around a wire?
options: The voltage across the wire creates magnetism.
A moving electric charge — i.e. an electric current.
The metal in the wire is naturally magnetic.
Metal heats up faster because it has more thermal energy to begin with.

mcqs.q: What happens to the current as it goes around a series circuit?
options: Current gets used up by each component as it flows around the circuit.
It stays the same at every point — current is conserved.
Current splits in half at the battery so each direction gets some.
The voltage across the wire creates magnetism.

mcqs.q: Why does a metal spoon in hot water heat up faster than a wooden one?
options: Metal heats up faster because it has a lower specific heat capacity, requiring less energy per degree.
The voltage across the wire creates magnetism.
Metal heats up faster because it has more thermal energy to begin with.
Metals have higher thermal conductivity, so heat is transferred more rapidly through them.
